introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub mark in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH paper are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Seconde passe faite : chaque page du PDF (pages 2 a 4 et les trois pages de cartes) a ete relue et comparee a chaque enonce transcrit (aucun ecart de texte, de numero ni de points) ; chaque question a ete resolue une seconde fois ; les lectures de carte (182909, 258897, 1164, 2586, 2297, gisement, aire) ont ete reverifiees sur des agrandissements avec un repere en croix : aucune correction necessaire.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Using specific examples, distinguish between:

(i) Push and pull factors of migration,
(ii) Rural and urban settlements,
(iii) Primary and Secondary industries.

(9 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three marks for each pair (the two meanings and a specific example).

**(i) Push and pull factors of migration**

| Push factors | Pull factors |
|---|---|
| Conditions in the **place of origin** that force or encourage people to leave: unemployment, poverty, poor soil or drought, war and insecurity, lack of schools and hospitals | Attractions of the **place of destination** that draw people there: jobs and better pay, schools, hospitals, electricity, security, entertainment |
| Example: people leave villages of the Far North because of drought, poor land and insecurity caused by armed attacks | Example: Douala and Yaounde attract migrants because of jobs in industry, trade and services, and better social facilities |

**(ii) Rural and urban settlements**

| Rural settlement | Urban settlement |
|---|---|
| A **small** settlement (a village or hamlet) with few people, in the countryside; most people are **farmers, fishermen or herders** (primary activities); few services | A **large** settlement (a town or city) with many people, high density and many buildings; people work in **industry, trade, administration and services**; many services (schools, hospitals, banks, markets) |
| Example: a village in the Western Highlands or on the coast with a school and a market | Example: Douala (industry and port) and Yaounde (the capital) |

**(iii) Primary and secondary industries**

| Primary industries | Secondary industries |
|---|---|
| They **extract or produce raw materials** directly from nature: farming, fishing, forestry, mining, oil extraction | They **process or manufacture** raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods |
| Example: cocoa farming, logging, oil production offshore | Example: sawmills and furniture making, cocoa processing, brewing, aluminium smelting at Edea |

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Briefly explain why in most Least Industrialised Countries (LICs) more people are engaged in agriculture yet their output is low.
(ii) Describe **THREE** things these nations can do to emerge.

(4+3=7 marks)

(Total = 20 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Many farmers, low output (4 marks, any four points).**

1. **Few other jobs:** there is little industry and few services, so most of the workforce depends on farming.
2. **Simple tools and methods:** farmers use the hoe and the cutlass, with little machinery, improved seeds, fertiliser or irrigation, so yields per person are low.
3. **Small farms and subsistence farming:** holdings are small and split among heirs, and much of the crop is eaten by the family, not sold.
4. **Dependence on the weather, pests and diseases:** crops fail in dry years and are lost to pests and diseases.
5. **Poor storage, roads and markets:** part of the harvest rots and farmers receive low prices. Low education and lack of credit also limit progress.

**(ii) Three things these nations can do to emerge (3 marks, one each with its description).**

1. **Industrialise and diversify the economy:** build factories to process local raw materials (cocoa, timber, cotton), which creates jobs and adds value to exports.
2. **Modernise agriculture:** give farmers credit, fertilisers, improved seeds, machinery and training, and build rural roads and storage so that output and income rise.
3. **Invest in education, health and infrastructure:** train a skilled workforce and build roads, electricity and water supply, which also attract foreign investors.
4. **Other answers:** good governance and fight against corruption, regional trade, reduction of debt.
